brief: Legacy over virality — 5 things founders get wrong about building something lasting.

slots.subtitle: Why the founders who build for decades ignore the playbook the rest of the world worships.

slots.body: We have confused motion with momentum. Lasting companies are not built in sprints; they are composed in patient, deliberate movements that compound in silence.
Founders mistake press coverage for product depth. A beautiful story without structural integrity collapses the moment the market stops applauding.
When the term sheet becomes the trophy, the architecture suffers. The best builders design for permanence, knowing liquidity is a byproduct, not a purpose.
Prestige hires signal status, but they rarely share the obsession. Legacy demands alignment more than it demands recognizable names or polished resumes.
Expansion without operational depth is a debt that accrues invisibly. The founders who endure reinvest in systems long before the world demands them.
A personal brand is not a substitute for institutional values. When the founder steps back, only codified principle keeps the compass true.
Legacy is not a milestone. It is the quiet result of refusing to trade tomorrow’s relevance for today’s applause.
